source.note: Scan without a text layer. National Senior Certificate paper (cover: NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE; running header: NSC). The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 15); PDF page n = printed page n. The cover states that the question paper consists of 14 pages, 1 information sheet and an answer book of 28 pages, which is not in this PDF. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.stem_md: A survey was conducted at a local supermarket relating the distance that shoppers lived from the store to the average number of times they shopped at the store in a week. The results are shown in the table below.

table.caption: Distance from the store and average number of times shopped per week
header: Distance from the store in km
rows: Average number of times shopped per week

questions.text_md: Use the scatter plot to comment on the strength of the relationship between the distance a shopper lived from the store and the average number of times she/he shopped at the store in a week.
Calculate the correlation coefficient of the data.
Calculate the equation of the least squares regression line of the data.
Use your answer at QUESTION 1.3 to estimate the average number of times that a shopper living $6$ km from the supermarket will visit the store in a week.
Sketch the least squares regression line on the scatter plot provided in the ANSWER BOOK.

questions.stem_md: The heights of $160$ learners in a school are measured. The height of the shortest learner is $1,39$ m and the height of the tallest learner is $2,21$ m. The heights are represented in the histogram below.

table.caption: Class frequencies as labelled on the printed histogram (the cumulative-frequency table itself is only in the answer book, which is not in this PDF)

questions.notes: Class frequencies 24, 71, 38, 23 and 4 are printed on the histogram bars (24+71+38+23+4=160). There is no bar in the interval starting at 1,1; the shortest recorded height is 1,39 m.

questions.text_md: Describe the skewness of the data.
Calculate the range of the heights.
questions.notes: Range from the given shortest and tallest heights (1,39 m and 2,21 m), not from the histogram class endpoints.

questions.text_md: Complete the cumulative frequency column in the table given in the ANSWER BOOK.
Draw an ogive (cumulative frequency curve) to represent the data on the grid provided in the ANSWER BOOK.
Eighty learners are less than $x$ metres in height. Estimate $x$.

questions.stem_md:
The person taking the measurements only had a $1,5$ m measuring tape available. In order to compensate for the short measuring tape, he decided to mount the tape on a wall at a height of $1$ m above the ground. After recording the measurements he discovered that the tape was mounted at $1,1$ m above the ground instead of $1$ m.

How does this error influence the following:

questions.text_md: Standard deviation of the data set

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\mathrm{A}(-7\,;\,2)$, $\mathrm{B}$, $\mathrm{C}(6\,;\,3)$ and $\mathrm{D}$ are the vertices of rectangle $\mathrm{ABCD}$. The equation of $\mathrm{AD}$ is $y=2x+16$. Line $\mathrm{AB}$ cuts the $y$-axis at $\mathrm{G}$. The $x$-intercept of line $\mathrm{BC}$ is $\mathrm{F}(p\,;\,0)$ and the angle of inclination of $\mathrm{BC}$ with the positive $x$-axis is $\alpha$. The diagonals of the rectangle intersect at $\mathrm{M}$.

questions.text_md: Write down the gradient of $\mathrm{BC}$ in terms of $p$.
Determine the equation of the circle passing through points $\mathrm{D}$, $\mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ in the form $(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}=r^{2}$.

If $\mathrm{AD}$ is shifted so that $\mathrm{ABCD}$ becomes a square, will $\mathrm{BC}$ be a tangent to the circle passing through points $\mathrm{A}$, $\mathrm{M}$ and $\mathrm{B}$, where $\mathrm{M}$ is now the intersection of the diagonals of the square $\mathrm{ABCD}$? Motivate your answer.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\mathrm{M}$ is the centre of the circle passing through $\mathrm{T}(3\,;\,7)$, $\mathrm{R}$ and $\mathrm{S}(5\,;\,2)$. $\mathrm{RT}$ is a diameter of the circle. $\mathrm{K}(a\,;\,b)$ is a point in the $4^{\text{th}}$ quadrant such that $\mathrm{KTL}$ is a tangent to the circle at $\mathrm{T}$.

questions.text_md: Determine the equation of the line $\mathrm{SR}$ in the form $y=mx+c$.

questions.stem_md: The equation of the circle above is $(x-9)^{2}+\left(y-6\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{2}=36\dfrac{1}{4}$.

questions.text_md: Calculate the length of $\mathrm{TR}$ in surd form.

Determine, **without using a calculator**, the value of EACH of the following in its simplest form:

questions.text_md: On the system of axes on which $f$ is drawn in the ANSWER BOOK, draw the graph of $g(x)=-\cos 2x$ for $x\in[-180^{\circ}\,;\,180^{\circ}]$. Clearly show all intercepts with the axes, the coordinates of the turning points and end points of the graph.
Write down the maximum value of $f(x)-3$.

questions.stem_md:
$\mathrm{E}$ is the apex of a pyramid having a square base $\mathrm{ABCD}$. $\mathrm{O}$ is the centre of the base. $\mathrm{E}\hat{\mathrm{B}}\mathrm{A}=\theta$, $\mathrm{AB}=3$ m and $\mathrm{EO}$, the perpendicular height of the pyramid, is $x$.
